Client has strict residency + audit requirements; leaning toward Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem option) but will accept Dedicated in NA region if residency controls documented.

Workload + requirements (customer-specified):
- Primary: real-time fraud scoring (per-transaction inference) — hard p95 target 30-50ms, p99 < 150ms.
- Secondary: batch embeddings generation overnight (high throughput window).
- Expected steady-state throughput: 300-500 TPS; burst up to 1200 TPS for promo periods.
- Model profile: medium-sized encoder-decoder + dense head; KV-cache warmup critical for latency.

Dedicated capacity / reserved GPU planning notes:
- Customer requests explicit GPU reservation (no noisy neighbors), predictable autoscale buffer of +20% for bursts.
- Redundancy: N+1 across AZs preferred; client requires clear failover time and expected latency hit during failover.
- Quantization/optimization permitted if quality regression <1% on fraud model eval set.

SLA terms under discussion (customer positions / negotiation points):
- Uptime target: customer asks 99.95% (<=22 minutes downtime/mo). Redwood initial proposal 99.9% (<=43 minutes/mo).
- Credit schedule: customer requests pro-rata credits starting at 100% of monthly fee for >2% downtime; incremental credits tiers requested for >0.5%, >1.0%, >2.0%.
- Maintenance windows: customer requires maintenance outside business hours (M-F 01:00-05:00 local) and advance notice 72 hours for planned work that affects availability.
- Emergency maintenance: client wants guaranteed option to opt-in to warm-standby during critical periods; cost delta TBD.
- Support response times: P1 initial response <= 1 hour, P2 <= 4 hours, on-call 24/7 for P1. Redwood standard is 1h for P1 but wants to hard-contract 30m for critical payment issues — counterproposal pending.

Security/compliance follow-ups:
- Need SOC2 attestation + KMS integration details.
- Data residency clause: log retention + tokenization path must remain within NA.
